prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Summary of the Liberal Democrats’ 2010 Manifesto: “Change That Works for You — Building a Fairer Britain” (≤500 words)

Core theme: Hard‑wiring fairness into national life by redistributing power—economic, social, political and financial—through four priorities:
- Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- A fair chance for every child
- A fair, green economy creating jobs
- A fair deal from politics and restored civil liberties

Fair taxes and fiscal credibility
- Raise the income tax personal allowance to £10,000 (c.£700 tax cut for most; 3.6m people lifted out of income tax), funded by: basic‑rate pension tax relief, aligning capital gains with income tax, anti‑avoidance, a per‑plane duty (with higher domestic rate where alternatives exist), and a 1% mansion tax on property value above £2m.
- Restore earnings link for the state pension (triple lock: earnings, prices, or 2.5%).
- Deficit plan: over £15bn annual savings identified from 2011–12; timing guided by economic conditions. Savings include: £400 cap on public sector pay rises (for two years), restricting tax credits, ending Child Trust Funds, a bank levy, scrapping ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint, cancelling Eurofighter Tranche 3B, prison reform (less short sentences), cutting quangos/Whitehall costs, IT procurement reform, and considering alternatives to like‑for‑like Trident replacement. Establish a cross‑party Council on Financial Stability and conduct a Comprehensive Spending Review.

Jobs, growth and green transition
- Break up banks (separate retail/investment), reform bonuses, get lending flowing, and create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges.
- One‑year green stimulus creating c.100,000 jobs: shipyard upgrades for offshore wind, £400 Eco Cash‑Back for home efficiency/microgeneration, school/public‑building efficiency, bringing 250,000 empty homes into use, bus scrappage.
- Create a UK Infrastructure Bank to mobilise private capital for energy/transport (including high‑speed rail, superfast broadband).
- Support enterprise by cutting red tape/gold‑plating, reforming business rates (site value), refocusing/scrapping weak RDAs, and backing mutuals/co‑ops.

Education and skills
- £2.5bn “Pupil Premium” targeted at disadvantaged pupils to cut class sizes/boost one‑to‑one support; stronger SEN diagnosis/support; improve teacher training.
- Slimmer curriculum and standards body; reform tests/league tables; allow 14–19 choices across schools/colleges; fair funding for FE.
- Scrap tuition fees over six years (immediate abolition for final‑year students); targeted bursaries; more foundation degrees and adult apprenticeships.

NHS and care
- Protect frontline care by cutting bureaucracy; integrate health and social care; elected Local Health Boards; patient entitlements to timely diagnosis/treatment; expand mental health/dementia support; curb alcohol harm; reduce air pollution; set up a cross‑party long‑term care commission and provide guaranteed respite for carers.

Families and consumers
- Shared parental leave and flexible working for all; child protection strengthened; youth services statutory; scrap default retirement age; fairer energy tariffs/social tariffs; PostBank; cap unfair financial charges; cut regulated rail fares.

Climate, environment and transport
- Zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; 40% of electricity from non‑carbon sources by 2020 (prioritise marine/offshore); block unabated coal; oppose new nuclear; national insulation programme; European Supergrid; zero‑waste goals; stronger biodiversity/water management; protect countryside access.
- Replace Air Passenger Duty with per‑plane duty; cancel Heathrow third runway; road pricing prep (revenue‑neutral); rural fuel discount.

Communities, crime, immigration, housing
- 3,000 more police funded by ID cards cut; reduce police bureaucracy; elected police authorities; restorative justice; presumption against <6‑month sentences.
- Firm but fair immigration: reintroduce exit checks; National Border Force; regional points‑based system; earned citizenship for long‑term undocumented residents pre‑2010; end child detention in asylum cases.
- Bring empty homes into use; enable council housebuilding; strengthen tenant/consumer protections.

Political reform and civil liberties
- Proportional representation (STV), reduce MPs by 150, fixed‑term parliaments, elected second chamber, written constitution via citizens’ convention, recall of MPs, cap donations at £10,000, lobbyist register, UK tax domicile for all parliamentarians/candidates.
- Freedom Bill: scrap ID cards/biometric passports, regulate CCTV, protect protest/free speech (libel reform), limit DNA retention, end mass communications data storage, reduce pre‑charge detention to 14 days, allow intercept evidence, scrap control orders.

International
- Pro‑EU leadership on climate and financial regulation; meet 0.7% aid by 2013; forest protection; IMF/WB reform; no like‑for‑like Trident; defence review; pay rise and better housing for lower ranks; responsible foreign policy (Afghanistan strategy, two‑state solution, inquiry into torture, arms trade controls, diplomatic approach to Iran).
